subject: UK residency attestation & TIA sprint (Medicore)
messages:
From: Emma Watson <emma.watson@medicore.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: UK residency attestation & TIA sequencing request

Soojin,

Appreciate the demo and the draft addendum. Our legal and infra teams reviewed the draft and surfaced three operational items we need resolved prior to signature: 

1) A short residency attestation describing where request metadata and ephemeral caches for UK-origin traffic are stored and whether those artifacts ever leave UK-hosted infrastructure.
2) A mapping of Redwood subprocessors that process telemetry or request metadata in the UK region (we attached the list of processors we care about). Please flag which of those are UK-edge and which, if any, replicate across borders.
3) A proposed TIA/DTIA delivery sprint tied to signature (what we expect immediately at sign, and what we will receive at 30/60/90 days).

Our procurement window targets signature by 2026-08-30. If you can provide the attestation and a subprocessor mapping by 08/23 we can push to procurement.

Thanks,
Emma Watson
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Medicore Health

Attachments: medicore-uk-addendum-draft-annotated.pdf (PDF, 240KB); redwood-subprocessors.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Watson <emma.watson@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: UK residency attestation & TIA sequencing request

Emma 

Thanks for the clear asks and the annotated draft. Quick answers so procurement has visibility: 

- Residency attestation: we can provide a one-paragraph attestation stating that for UK-origin requests routed to our UK region, request metadata (headers, routing tags) and ephemeral KV caches are retained on UK-hosted compute and local ephemeral storage; they are not replicated to non-UK regions except for operator-controlled debug snapshots that are pseudonymized and require multi-person access to unmask. I'll draft the exact wording and share it today.

- Subprocessor mapping: attaching our exported subprocessor registry. Jonas, can you mark which processors handle telemetry in the UK-edge and confirm if any replicate telemetry off-shore for downstream analytics?

- TIA/DTIA sprint: our standard sequencing is: 
  * Day 0 (post-sign): signed UK Addendum, confirmation of TIA scope and primary contacts; high-level subprocessor list.
  * Day 30: delivery of technical safeguards packet (network diagrams, data flow summary, encryption at rest/in transit details, KMS key locations) and per-subprocessor evidence where available.
  * Day 90: full audit package including sample logs, attestation letters from select subprocessors, and remediation plan for any gaps.

We can compress Day 30 to Day 15 for critical accounts if Medicore needs it, but that requires a legal exception and prioritized engineering runbook. If you confirm the 08/30 signature target, we will aim to deliver the evidence packet by 08/23.

If helpful, Marissa and Jonas can join a 30-min call tomorrow 10:00-11:30 UK time to walk the list.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-subprocessors.csv (export from registry)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: RE: UK residency attestation & TIA sequencing request

Team 

Quick legal notes / items we should include before sending to Medicore: 

1) Attestation language: keep it operational and not contractual - a single paragraph that states facts about compute locality, default retention window for caches, and exception handling for debug snapshots. Avoid promising "never" if there are lawful requests or emergency fallbacks.

Proposed one-paragraph (draft): "For requests originating from the United Kingdom and routed to Redwood's UK region, transient request metadata (including HTTP headers and routing tags) and KV cache artifacts are stored on UK-hosted compute and local ephemeral storage. These artifacts are retained for a short operational window for request processing and are not routinely replicated outside the UK. Operator-initiated debug snapshots may be transferred out-of-region for incident investigation; such transfers are pseudonymized and require multi-person authorization."

2) Subprocessor evidence: prepare a CSV with the following columns: processor name, function, region(s), evidence type (SAA/SOC2/contract), whether UK-edge telemetry is processed, and contact. Jonas: can you populate region and "replicates off-shore" flags by EOD?

3) TIA content checklist: Medicore will expect at minimum network diagrams, KMS key location(s), ingress/egress flow logs retention, syslog sampling guidance, and a list of per-subprocessor attestations (or expected delivery timeframe). Add "sample log slices" to Day 90 deliverable.

4) DocuSign cadence: if procurement wants sign by 08/30, we need to freeze language by 08/24 to allow doc cycle + counterparty review.

I attached the legal evidence checklist and a redline I started against their annotated PDF. Once Jonas updates the subprocessor flags, we can bundle and send.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-legal-evidence-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB); medicore-uk-addendum-draft-annotated.pdf (annotated)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Emma Watson <emma.watson@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:05:00 +0100
Subject: RE: UK residency attestation & TIA sequencing request - subprocessor flags

Emma / team,

I pulled the registry rows that match Medicore's CSV and annotated the "region" and "replicates_offshore" flags. Summary: 

- EdgeTelemetry Ltd. (telemetry collector): UK-edge, does not replicate off-shore by default (replication disabled for UK tenants).
- LogStream EU (log aggregation): EU primary, replicates to a central analytics cluster in the EU; UK telemetry is retained in the UK region and only metadata references are sent to EU for billing/rollup.
- AnalyticsNow (downstream analytics): Cross-border processing (UK->EU), but we have contractual SCCs and an IDTA in place (evidence attached).
- CDNProbe (edge caching): global; only request headers are sampled at the edge and are pseudonymized before being sent to central ops in the US for network troubleshooting. We flagged this as a potential discussion point.

Action items: 
- Soojin: finalize the one-paragraph attestation and include the phrase "operator-initiated debug snapshots are pseudonymized and require multi-person authorization."
- Marissa: include the SCC/IDTA references in the evidence packet and flag CDNProbe as a discussion item for legal.
- Delivery: I'll export the annotated CSV and sample evidence PDF by EOD.

Jonas
Lead Infra Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: registry-annotated-medicore.csv (CSV, 8KB); analyticsnow-idta.pdf (PDF, 72KB)
